variants.name: Hand-written keyset iterator with opaque cursor
variants.idiom_name: cursor value type + base64url codec + input iterator over keyset pages
variants.implementation_notes: The C++ standard library has no pagination type, so the realization is a small cursor value type, a base64url codec and a lazy page source: a function or input iterator that issues a keyset statement through the database client (libpq, sqlite3, libpqxx) or an RPC stub, exposes std::vector<Row> pages, and derives the next token from the last row of the previous page. A C++11 lambda-based iterator or an explicit Page/Tokens struct is enough; the classic hand-written form stays justified whenever you own both the API contract and the data store, while google-cloud-cpp's StreamRange covers the case of consuming Google-style RPCs.
pitfalls: Iterator and lifetime: a page-buffer iterator must not outlive the page buffer it references, and capturing a page object by reference in an async completion handler is the C++ equivalent of a dangling cursor.

Composite cursor comparisons are easy to get wrong by hand: the predicate must mirror the ORDER BY exactly, including per-column direction and NULL placement, which std::tuple comparison alone does not express.

variants.name: google-cloud-cpp StreamRange over page_token RPCs
variants.implementation_notes: For list RPCs wrapped by google-cloud-cpp the library provides the iteration: the request carries a page_token (a plain std::string the library passes through) and the call returns google::cloud::StreamRange<T>, a move-only lazy range of StatusOr<T> that fetches subsequent pages for you; the range ends on a non-OK status. Use this variant when the collection lives behind a Google-style API; use the hand-written keyset iterator when the collection is your own database.
pitfalls: A transient backend failure ends the StreamRange like the end of the collection: check the last StatusOr, or the loop silently reports a truncated iteration as complete.
The library does not validate your request: changing filter or ordering fields while re-using next_page_token asks a different question and yields an incoherent sequence.
